title: Interaction Testing on Non-State-Changing Methods
pattern: Verifying interactions (using mocks or spies) on non-state-changing query operations, such as assertions that a data read method was invoked.
why_bad: It checks how a system arrived at its result rather than verifying that the result is correct [518]. It adds test brittleness because read interactions represent internal data-flow patterns that are likely to change [529].
detection: Using mocking expectations or spies to assert that getter, database query, or read-only collaborator methods were invoked during execution [530].
counterexample: Verifying a state-changing operation (such as adding a record or writing to a socket) where the interaction itself is the primary side-effect being verified [530].
fix: Verify only state-changing operations via interaction testing, and use state assertions (verifying final return values or mutations) for non-state-changing operations [518, 529].
source: *   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Interaction Testing on Non-State-Changing Functions" (p. 275-276) [518, 529, 530]
